newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch TV producer Endemol set for bourse debut.
newsitem.headline: Dutch TV producer Endemol set for bourse debut.

text.p: Up to a third of the shares in one of Europe's biggest television production firms, Endemol Entertainment Holding NV, will be floated on the Amsterdam bourse next month, ABN AMRO Bank said on Thursday.
ABN AMRO Rothschild will act as global co-ordinator for a combined primary and secondary offering of up to 9.69 million ordinary Endemol shares at 44 to 48 guilders per share, it said.
Endemol was formed in 1994 by a merger of the production companies of co-chairmen Joop van den Ende and John de Mol.
Its net profit rose 38 percent to 60.5 million guilders ($35 million) in the financial year to July 31, 1996 on a turnover of 642.4 million guilders.
The company expects net profit to rise by 15 to 20 percent in the current 1996/97 financial year and predicts that both sales and profits will double within five years.
Endemol already generates some 40 percent of its turnover outside the Netherlands and plans further expansion abroad.
Subscriptions to the offering will open on Friday and are expected to close on November 6, with the shares expected to be traded on the Amsterdam bourse from November 7.
A book-building system will be used, in which investors can indicate the number of shares they want and the price they are willing to pay.

Endemol will issue 4.4 million new shares for the offering, with existing shareholders offering up to 5.28 million of their shares. The issuing syndicate has the right to buy an additional 1.45 million shares from existing shareholders if there is sufficient demand from investors.
If this option is exercised, some 33 percent of Endemol's share capital will be tradeable on the Amsterdam bourse, ABN AMRO said.
At present Joop van den Ende and John de Mol own some 95 percent of Endemol's shares. ($1=1.708 Guilder)
